title: Cloudflare Overview
description: All Cloudflare services for the cloudless.gr account on one screen: edge traffic, tunnels, Workers, and R2. Sources: cloudflare-exporter (GraphQL analytics, 5-min window) + cloudflared native /metrics. Free-plan datasets only — per-minute edge TTFB and firewall-event detail are plan-gated and absent by design.

panels.title: Edge requests by hostname
panels.description: Requests hitting Cloudflare's edge for each hostname in the zone, per scrape window. Watch for sudden drops on expected hosts (tunnel/origin down) or spikes on unexpected hosts (abuse, misconfigured clients).

panels.title: Edge response status mix
panels.description: Edge response codes returned to clients, grouped by class. A rising 5xx line means the edge (or origin through the tunnel) is failing — check tunnel HA and the origin service below. Sustained 4xx growth is usually probing or auth failures, not an outage.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of edge requests served from Cloudflare cache vs. sent to origin. Higher is better — every miss costs origin CPU and tunnel bandwidth. Low values are normal here since most hosts are dynamic apps behind tunnels.

panels.title: Threats today
panels.description: Requests Cloudflare classified as threats for the current UTC day (WAF decisions, bot scores, reputation). Sourced from the free daily dataset — a spike usually means scanning/bot floods, not a breach; blocked traffic never reaches origin.

panels.title: Origin response time (ms)
panels.description: How fast origins answer through the edge — p50/p95/p99 quantiles over the scrape window. p99 climbing while p50 stays flat = a few slow endpoints (check which host via the misses panel). Everything above ~1s p95 deserves a look at the origin service.

panels.title: Daily traffic totals
panels.description: Full-day request, bandwidth and page-view totals per UTC day (free 1-day dataset). Use this for trend: growth here is real reach; the 5-minute panels above are for debugging. Bandwidth matters for the 10GB R2/egress-adjacent limits on free plans.

panels.title: Requests by country
panels.description: Client countries hitting the edge in the window. Confirms the audience is who we think it is; an unexpected dominant country usually means crawler traffic or a misconfigured integration rather than real users.

panels.title: Tunnel HA connections
panels.description: Active cloudflared connections to Cloudflare's edge per host (.128 = social-auto host, .130 = omv-ha). Cloudflared keeps 4 HA connections when healthy; anything <4 means the tunnel is degraded — public hostnames behind it may flap.

panels.title: Tunnel request rate
panels.description: Requests proxied through each cloudflared daemon per second. Correlates with edge traffic — if edge requests are up but tunnel requests are flat, responses are being served from cache or failing before the origin.

panels.title: Tunnel response errors
panels.description: Errors returned by origins through the tunnel (connection refused, timeouts, 5xx from the app). Should stay near zero; a sustained rise points at the origin service behind that hostname, not at Cloudflare.

panels.title: Worker invocations
panels.description: Invocations per Worker script and status (success/exceeded/errors) in each window. This is where Workers-AI-adjacent traffic shows up too — postiz-ai-proxy, mail-ingest and the carousel fan-out run on the same free 100k-requests/day budget. Watch total volume against that cap.

panels.title: Worker errors & p99 CPU
panels.description: Left axis: error count per script — anything nonzero repeatedly is a bug to ship a fix for. Right axis: p99 CPU microseconds — Workers free tier allows ~10ms CPU per request; scripts trending toward that get throttled.

panels.title: R2 storage per bucket
panels.description: Current object storage footprint per bucket. Free tier: 10GB/month storage + 1M writes/10M reads. datalake-bucket holds the heaviest data — if it approaches the cap, prune old exports before Cloudflare starts billing or rejecting writes.

panels.title: R2 operations
panels.description: Class-A (write) and Class-B (read) API operations per bucket in the window. Free quota: 1M Class-A + 10M Class-B per month — a runaway exporter or sync job shows up here before it shows up on a bill.

panels.title: Collector status
panels.description: 1 = the last GraphQL poll of the Cloudflare account succeeded; 0 = the API token or a dataset failed. If this drops, all Cloudflare panels above go stale while infrastructure panels (tunnels, origin) keep updating.
